name: Template — copy this file to start your jurisdiction
summary: A worked example of the overlay format, not a description of any real place. Copy this file to data/jurisdictions/<your-id>.json, replace every note with the statute, tariff, or ordinance that actually governs where you are, and open a pull request. Overlays add local context to the shared requirements; they never change or remove one.

maintainers.name: Your name or organisation
maintainers.org: Town, county, agency, NGO, or law school clinic
maintainers.contact: A public contact — an email alias, an issue thread, or a repository handle

s1-r2.note: Replace with your state's authority for developer-funded review escrow, and any cap on what may be charged. Some states authorise this explicitly for major site plan review; others allow it only by agreement; a few do not permit it at all. Say which one applies here.
s1-r2.citation: Cite the enabling statute or the appellate decision, with its section number.

s1-r5.note: Replace with the notice statute that governs rezoning and conditional use hearings here: publication interval, mailed-notice radius, sign posting, and what a defective notice does to an approval.
s1-r5.citation: Cite the statute and the leading case on defective notice in this state.

s3-r2.note: Replace with how this state treats exactions and conditions on legislative approvals, and whether a development agreement is authorised by statute here at all.
s3-r2.citation: Cite the development agreement enabling act, if one exists.

s4-r5.note: Replace with the water provider's actual declared drought stages, by name, and the ordinance or tariff that assigns curtailment priority between industrial cooling and domestic service.
s4-r5.citation: Cite the drought management plan and the section that sets the priority order.

s7-r6.note: Replace with the docket number of this state's large-load tariff proceeding, whether it is open, and who may intervene without counsel.
s7-r6.citation: Cite the commission docket and the intervention deadline.

s9-r2.note: Replace with what financial security this jurisdiction may lawfully require, in what form, and whether decommissioning security for a non-energy use survives a challenge here.
s9-r2.citation: Cite the statute or ordinance authorising the security.
